slides.html: 1. Value Function Iteration
slides.title: 1. Value Function Iteration

slides.html:
The Bellman Equation

V(k)=\max_{k'\in\Gamma(k)}\{u(k,k')+\beta V(k')\}
  • tomorrow's problem looks like today's: summarise it by V
  • Bellman operator (TW)(k)=\max_{k'}\{u(k,k')+\beta W(k')\}
  • the value function is a fixed point: V=TV
slides.title: The Bellman Equation

slides.html:
Blackwell's Conditions

T is a contraction of modulus \beta if

  1. monotonicity: V\le W\Rightarrow TV\le TW
  2. discounting: T(V+c)\le TV+\beta c

Proof: V\le W+\|V-W\|\Rightarrow TV\le TW+\beta\|V-W\|; swap V,W.
slides.title: Blackwell's Conditions

slides.html:
Contraction Mapping Theorem

A contraction on a complete space has a unique fixed point V^*, and V_{n+1}=TV_n converges:

\|V_n-V^*\|\le\beta^n\|V_0-V^*\|,\qquad \|V_n-V^*\|\le\frac{\beta}{1-\beta}\|V_n-V_{n-1}\|
  • start from any V_0; stop when iterates are close
  • the nearer \beta is to 1, the slower
slides.title: Contraction Mapping Theorem

slides.html: 2–4. Brownian Motion, Itô, GBM
slides.title: 2–4. Brownian Motion, Itô, GBM

slides.html:
The Itô Integral

\int_0^Tf\,dW=\lim\sum f(t_i)(W_{t_{i+1}}-W_{t_i})\quad\text{(left endpoint)}

\displaystyle\int_0^TW\,dW=\tfrac12W_T^2-\tfrac12T — the extra -\tfrac12T comes from (dW)^2=dt.
slides.title: The Itô Integral

slides.html:
Itô's Lemma

For dS=a\,dt+\sigma\,dW, with (dt)^2=dt\,dW=0, (dW)^2=dt:

dF=\Big(F_t+aF_s+\tfrac12\sigma^2F_{ss}\Big)dt+\sigma F_s\,dW
  • F=W^2: dF=dt+2W\,dW
  • F=3+t+e^{W}: dF=(1+\tfrac12e^W)dt+e^WdW
slides.title: Itô's Lemma

slides.html: 5. Dynamic Hedging and the PDE
slides.title: 5. Dynamic Hedging and the PDE

slides.html:
No Arbitrage Gives the PDE

dP=rP\,dt implies

F_t+rSF_s+\tfrac12\sigma^2F_{ss}-rF=0,\qquad F(S_T,T)=\max(S_T-K,0)
  • \mu has disappeared: no dependence on risk preferences
  • rebalancing is dynamic and self-financing

F=SN(d_1)-Ke^{-r(T-t)}N(d_2), hedge ratio F_s=N(d_1).
slides.title: No Arbitrage Gives the PDE

slides.html: 6–8. Changing the Measure
slides.title: 6–8. Changing the Measure

slides.html:
Many Periods

\frac{S_t}{R_f^{\,t}}=E_t^Q\Big[\frac{S_{t+i}}{R_f^{\,t+i}}\Big]\qquad\text{a martingale under }Q

Price of a payoff C_T: C_0=E^Q[C_T/R_f^T].
slides.title: Many Periods

slides.html:
Girsanov's Theorem

If W is a P-BM and E\exp(\tfrac12\int\gamma^2)<\infty:

  • \dfrac{dQ}{dP}=\exp\Big(-\displaystyle\int\gamma\,dW-\tfrac12\int\gamma^2dt\Big)
  • \widetilde W_t=W_t+\int_0^t\gamma_s\,ds is a Q-BM

Changing the drift = changing the measure: replace dW+\gamma\,dt by d\widetilde W.
slides.title: Girsanov's Theorem

slides.html:
Pricing Recipe

  1. write the SDE, choose \gamma so the drift becomes r
  2. price under Q:
    • terminal payoff: C_0=E^Q[e^{-rT}C_T]
    • path-dependent: Monte Carlo and average

\gamma=(\mu-r)/\sigma is the market price of risk; dS=rS\,dt+\sigma S\,d\widetilde W.
slides.title: Pricing Recipe

slides.html:
Two Routes, One Answer

e^{-rt}F(S_t,t) is a Q-martingale \Rightarrow zero drift \Rightarrow the PDE.

Hedging Martingale
tool Itô + no arbitrage Girsanov + E^Q
output PDE E^Q[e^{-rT}C_T]
good for closed forms path dependence
slides.title: Two Routes, One Answer

slides.html: 9–10. Money and Central Banking
slides.title: 9–10. Money and Central Banking

slides.html:
Bank Bookkeeping

  • loan: asset +L, deposit +L — lending creates deposits
  • repayment destroys deposits
  • default: written off against equity
slides.title: Bank Bookkeeping

slides.html:
Central Bank Tools

  • open-market operations: buy or sell securities for reserves
  • discount window: lend at the discount rate
  • repo / reverse repo with a haircut
  • moving government deposits between the central bank and banks
slides.title: Central Bank Tools

slides.html:
Quantitative Easing

  • short rate at its lower bound
  • buy long-term assets at large scale, creating reserves
  • aim: lower long yields, ease credit
slides.title: Quantitative Easing

slides.html:
Review

Bellman contraction → value function. Itô: (dW)^2=dt. Black–Scholes: hedge or change the measure. Money: loans create deposits, reserves settle, the central bank sets the price of reserves.
slides.title: Review
